longForm.heroHook: Compact enough for the flow cabinet. Smart enough to count cells for you.
longForm.heroLead: Cell culture work happens in a sterile hood, on a schedule, usually more than once a day. A microscope that doesn't fit the cabinet, or that demands a manual cell count every single time, is friction the workflow doesn't need. Primovert is built to remove exactly that. The base model handles brightfield and phase contrast for living cells, unstained, exactly as they are. Add iLED fluorescence and GFP-labeled cells become visible too, switching contrast directly at the stand, no separate fluorescence unit to bolt on. Go one step further with Primovert digital, and a built-in 5 MP CMOS camera paired with AI-based analysis in ZEISS Labscope counts cells, measures confluency, and shares results, all with one click. Every version is compact enough to fit inside a laminar flow cabinet, so sterile technique never has to compete with getting a good look at the culture. What it replaces: manual cell counting and a separate fluorescence setup. What it adds with digital: one-click AI cell analysis and instant sharing beyond the sterile workspace. Where it lives: the bench, or the hood, whichever the culture actually needs.

faqs.question: What is the Zeiss Axiovert 5 used for?
faqs.answer: It's an inverted microscope for cell culture and research, supporting DIC, iHMC, phase contrast, brightfield, and multichannel fluorescence on one stand.

faqs.question: Does it need a computer to operate?
faqs.answer: No. In standalone configuration, an Axiocam camera and on-screen display run the system independently, saving images directly to USB.

faqs.question: How does multichannel fluorescence work?
faqs.answer: Paired with Colibri 3 LED illumination and any ZEISS microscope camera, select the channels for UV, blue, green, and red excitation, then press Snap. The system automatically adjusts exposure, acquires each channel, switches wavelengths, and delivers a single overlaid image with a scale bar embedded in the file metadata.

faqs.question: What contrast techniques are available?
faqs.answer: DIC, improved Hoffman Modulation Contrast (iHMC), phase contrast, and brightfield, in transmitted light, combined with multichannel fluorescence.

faqs.question: Can it handle large culture vessels?

faqs.question: Is AI-based cell analysis available?

faqs.question: What software options are available?
faqs.answer: Three configuration paths: standalone with an Axiocam and on-screen display, ZEISS Labscope for connected and multichannel fluorescence imaging, or ZEISS ZEN for advanced research-grade analysis.

faqs.question: Can the microscope be upgraded later?
faqs.answer: Yes, both hardware and software are upgradeable, so the stand can adapt as work requirements change rather than needing replacement.

faqs.question: How is Axiovert 5 different from Axiovert 5 digital?

Axiovert 5 digital integrates the camera and fluorescence system into a closed, all-in-one unit with one additional fluorescence channel and no external camera or light source decisions to make.

faqs.question: How is it different from Primovert?
faqs.answer: Primovert is a compact microscope built specifically to fit a laminar flow cabinet, covering brightfield and phase contrast, with fluorescence and AI analysis available on specific versions. AI Sample Finder automates the routine setup steps. Sample carrier detection, focus adjustment, and sample region identification, all handled automatically.
Time to image drops from minutes to seconds. The direct, stated result of removing manual sample-finding and focus steps.
Wizards guide experimental setup. Selecting the right imaging modality for the application becomes intuitive rather than a re-learned process each time.
Acquired images combine with electron microscopy and other modalities. Correlative workflows supported, not siloed.
Fast switchable light sources and filters. Highest spectral flexibility and speed, without slowing the workflow down.
Camera selection matched to the application. Sensitivity, resolution, and speed chosen for what the experiment actually needs.
Automatic focus maintenance for long-term imaging. Keeps samples in focus across extended sessions without manual intervention.
Automatic objective adaptation to the sample. The system adjusts rather than requiring manual reconfiguration.
Apotome 3 available for optical sectioning. Structured illumination removes out-of-focus light, delivering high-contrast images even from thicker specimens.
Autoimmersion Module available for Axio Observer 7. Automated, hands-free water immersion, removing both the tedium and the real risk of user error damaging data or the microscope.
Definite Focus 3 compensates for focus drift. Multi-day, multi-position time-lapse experiments stay sharp and high-contrast throughout.
Viluma 5 and 7 LED light sources for fluorescence. Fast illumination reducing cross-stimulation while increasing contrast and signal-to-noise ratio.
Xylis white light LED source. High, reproducible output with no warm-up time across its entire lifespan.
Virtual filter technology. A wide range of excitation and emission combinations, with high excitation intensity and extremely fast switching.
Duolink enables simultaneous spectral imaging. Two spectrally separated channels captured together, high-speed, through ZEN software.
Autocorr objectives adjust to the sample via a ZEN software slider. Crisp contrast maintained even deep inside the specimen.
Guided by ZEISS Microscopy Copilot. An AI assistant aware of the exact microscope configuration and available ZEN Toolkits.
Field number of 23 mm for large field of view imaging. Referenced specifically in the live-cell culture application example.

body: Microscopes keep getting more automated on the imaging side, but placing the sample, adjusting focus, and identifying the relevant region on a carrier have stayed stubbornly manual, small steps repeated at the start of every session, every sample, every day.

AI Sample Finder removes that sequence. It detects the sample carrier automatically, adjusts focus, and locates the sample region without operator input, and Zeiss states the effect directly: time to image drops from minutes to just seconds. Across a lab running dozens of samples a day, that isn't a convenience feature, it's a genuine change in how much research actually fits into a working session.
